quote: An enabled service with missing deadlines fails before listening, with the migration remedy in the error.
Under the single-writer condition in docs/operations.md, missing values are written together before HTTP listens. An unsuccessful write prevents startup and leaves the previous snapshot readable.
Enabled startup against a stored ticket missing due fails before HTTP listens, and leaves the file untouched. After migration, enabled startup serves the durable values.
The service file owner preserves existing assigned deadlines and fills missing ones from persisted creation and priority, making a whole-file save before service availability.
On startup with DATA_FILE, save any missing deadlines atomically before the service listens.
For pre-existing records without a deadline, use the record's current stored priority and creation instant, then save before serving.
Backfill runs even with the display flag off and saves before requests are served.
Before exposure, save any missing deadlines without changing ticket IDs, ordinary fields, audit, outbox or sequence counters.
Before listening, fill missing due values using each record’s own creation time and persisted priority, then atomically save them when DATA_FILE is set.
An offline operator command uses the same hour overrides on stored creation and priority for tickets missing due.
Backfill missing deadlines from each ticket's stored creation and priority, preserve previously assigned dates and save before serving.
The owning service writes the result using its normal atomic file replacement before accepting requests, regardless of flag state. A failed write prevents startup.

The service computes missing deadlines from each stored creation time and stored priority even when HTTP exposure is off. On a data-file start it completes the durable write before accepting requests.
A startup requiring migration completes the atomic save before listening.
Verify 2025-09-02 08:00 UTC is on disk before the listener is available.

With DATA_FILE configured, startup fills missing due times from each row's stored created time and priority, retains due on previously migrated rows, and writes the data before serving. This happens even when due visibility is off.
Startup over an old file saves the complete upgrade before serving.
Persist atomically before enabled service starts answering, with a documented offline production preparation command for completing the file before setting the gate.
On startup with a data file, use each legacy ticket's recorded creation time and priority to set its missing due. Commit the complete snapshot atomically before listening.
Enabled startup refuses a persistent file containing tickets missing due.

Operators stop the sole writer and run the backfill before enabling. Existing tickets without due use their stored creation time and priority. An enabled service refuses an incomplete configured file.
An operator prepares the existing file with its writer stopped.
On startup, assign deadlines only to tickets still missing them using their persisted created timestamp and priority. When there is a data file, finish an atomic version-1 save before listening.
An enabled service with a missing due in a saved ticket refuses startup before listening and gives operators the migration command.
